title: Madd 'arid lis-sukun and madd leen: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
source: Written for quran/y9 lesson 2 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Madd 'arid lis-sukun and madd leen rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 2. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Stopping changes the word
points: At a stop the last letter becomes sakin
A madd letter before it may lengthen
Only when stopping, never when continuing

panels.title: Madd leen
points: و or ي sakinah after fathah
Next letter sakin only because we stop

head: Not this
This
rows: Changing the 'arid length at every ayah end
Choose 2, 4 or 6 and keep it for the whole recitation

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)
a soft و or ي sakinah after fathah

questions.q: Recite 74:40 to 45 stopping at each ayah end, keeping 4 counts on every 'arid.
questions.a: 'Arid (4 counts) on يَتَسَآءَلُونَ, ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ, ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ, ٱلْمِسْكِينَ, ٱلْخَآئِضِينَ; none on سَقَرَ (no madd letter before the raa).

questions.q: Ending audit (pupil PDF): for 74:38 to 56, mark which ayah endings give 'arid lis-sukun when stopping. Today's rota group recites 74:31 to 37.
questions.a: 'Arid at 74:39, 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49. None at 74:38, 42, 50 to 56 (no madd letter before the last letter, or taa marbutah).

questions.q: Extend: find a madd leen at the end of an ayah in Quraysh.
Stretch: why can 'arid never be less than 2 counts?
questions.a: It is built on a madd letter, which always has its natural 2 counts; stopping can only add to it.
A) 2 counts (tabi'i). 'Arid only exists when stopping; joined, it is a natural madd of 2.

questions.q: Madd leen is a و or ي sakinah after ...
Think again: ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ (74:41): when you continue it is 2 counts; when you stop it can be 6. Why does stopping change it?
questions.a: Stopping makes the last letter sakin; a madd letter followed by a sukoon can stretch (2, 4 or 6).
